name: Brain, sleep and mood
about: Sleep and mood are the first things to slip under isolation, confinement and a shifted day-night cycle, and they drag everything else down with them.

name: Heart and circulation
about: Without gravity, blood and fluid move towards the head and the heart works against less load. Heart rate and blood pressure show how the circulation is adapting.

name: Lungs and oxygen
about: A closed cabin can build up carbon dioxide and its air is all you have. Blood oxygen is the quick check.

name: Blood sugar and energy
about: Spaceflight changes how the body handles sugar. Diet, stress, poor sleep and less muscle use all push it.

name: Body temperature
about: Body heat is harder to shed without convection, and fever is the first sign of infection in a crew that cannot leave.

name: Kidneys, fluids and salts
about: Fluid shifts and low water intake raise the risk of dehydration and kidney stones. The kidneys also keep the blood's salts in balance.

name: Liver
about: The liver processes nutrients and medication. Its enzymes in the blood show strain.

name: Bones
about: Weight-bearing bones lose about 1% to 1.5% of their mineral density per month in microgravity unless they are loaded by exercise.

name: Muscle and body mass
about: Muscles that no longer carry your weight shrink quickly. Body mass and exercise time track it.
